vocational

/voh-KAY-shuh-nuhl/ - the stress falls on KAY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Vocational means related to training for a specific trade or occupation.

The prison's vocational workshop teaches carpentry and small-engine repair, and graduates leave with union cards as well as release papers.

Example

After twenty years at a desk, Hal enrolled in a night vocational course in heating and cooling repair. Two winters later he had traded the cubicle for a service van, a toolbox, and a waiting list of customers who greeted him by name.

Vocational has narrowed from its root: today it almost always describes education aimed at a specific trade - welding, plumbing, dental assisting - rather than a felt calling. The word points at the training, not the pull.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

occupational: Occupational describes what belongs to a job someone already holds — its hazards, its injuries, its therapy and licensing. Vocational looks the other way: training that prepares you for a trade you do not yet have. An occupational injury happens on the job; a vocational course comes before the job exists.

hands-on: Hands-on describes how you learn: by doing the task rather than reading about it. Vocational describes what the learning is for: one specific trade or occupation. A chemistry lab is hands-on without being vocational, and a vocational bookkeeping course can be taught straight from a textbook.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

academic: centered on scholarly study

bookish: devoted to books over practice

Where it sits · how narrowly the learning targets one job — general → applied → vocational

general vs. vocational: A general education surveys a little of everything; vocational training aims every hour at one trade.

applied vs. vocational: Applied courses point knowledge toward practice; vocational goes further, training you to walk straight onto one specific job.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — voc-

Root — voc-: to call; voice

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act or state of

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Voc- (to call) + -ation (act or state of) + -al (relating to) = relating to one's calling. The word originally meant schooling for the work you were 'called' to do; modern English narrowed it to trade training. Its parent, vocation, still keeps the older warmth - see that card for the difference.

Use the root in a new word: vocal

Use the root in a new word: vocal: The senator was vocal about the bridge repairs, giving voice to the complaint at every meeting.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral / administrative

Vocational is the course-catalog word for trade-focused training; it carries no feeling. Its parent vocation still means a felt calling - do not swap them. If the contrast is with scholarly schooling, academic is the standard opposite number.
